newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - LVMH move clears air at Guinness.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - LVMH move clears air at Guinness.

text.p: A decision by LVMH Moet Hennessey Louis Vuitton to reduce its shareholding in Guinness by a third removes an uncertainty that has dogged Guinness shares, said Phil Yea, finance director in an interview.

"From time to time there has been speculation whether LVMH was going to be a seller of stock. Clearly by selling a third of its shares the scope for such discussion in the future is much reduced," Guinness' Yea said. "It's helpful in that it brings some clarity. I don't think management has been distracted by it. It's been more of an issue for the market."
Guinness shares were off 3p at 431p at 1425 GMT, after falling to 414p in early trade -- the price at which LVMH sold its 135 million Guinness shares.
Guinness itself bought 2.3 percent of the stock at a cost of 182 million pounds helping the shares stage a recovery.

It remains unclear how much LVMH made on the sale given that its initial 12 percent holding in Guinness was acquired in 1988 at an undisclosed price and then subsequent parcels were bought over the next two years. But the exchange rate factor would have produced a significant gain -- the pound has risen from 7.5 franc on November 17, 1995 to 9.04 franc today. Guinness shares were at 600p in May 1992 and reached a low of 402p in October 1993. The company's shares have underpeformed the sector by about 10 percent over the last five years and underperformed the all-share index by some 50 percent.
The company reported its highest pretax profits to date of 956 million pounds for the full year ended December 31, 1991.

A trading statement from the company on Wednesday caused some brokers to upgrade their estimates for 1996 profits by some 10 million to 970 million but downgrade their 1997 forecasts by as much as 50 million to 940 million due to sterling's strength on foreign exchange markets.
